newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New Dutch options trading system delayed again.
newsitem.headline: New Dutch options trading system delayed again.

text.p: The introduction of a new trading system at Amsterdam's European Options Exchange (EOE) will be delayed again because the new system is impractical and must be changed, an EOE spokesman said on Thursday.

"We have concluded that it is physically too difficult for market makers simultaneously to work on the floor and the electronic system at the same time," said Alexander van Drooge, head of public relations at the EOE.
The proposed system, Switch, aims to give the EOE a competitive edge over its rivals by combining the versatility of the open outcry system with the speed of a screen system.
Originally scheduled to begin in mid-1996, the new system will not begin until an unspecified time next year.
The impracticality of market makers shouting on the floor and keying in numbers at the same time has forced the EOE to put forward two plans to members.
The first is to split option trading into screen trading for small transactions and open outcry for large orders. The EOE would rely on arbitrage to narrow any differences in prices.
The second system would employ EOE overseers to fit best offers to best bids, whether on the screen or the floor.
"We expect the members to decide in a couple of months," said van Drooge.

The EOE said it will bring in changes gradually and expected to introduce the electronic delivery of orders by the end of the year. However, the fundamental changes to the trading system will not take place until 1997.
"We cannot say how long it will take. Anyway, we don't want a big bang. We want a step-by-step implementation," said van Drooge.
